Additionally, for r ∈ { 3 , … , 7 } r\in\{3,\dots,7\} , when the coloring is not proper, its loss seems to almost always take the same one or two precise values. This trend becomes especially apparent for r r close to 7 7 . For example, for r = 7 r=7 , a proper coloring is found 91 91 times, but in all nine remaining times, the loss is either 64 64 or 96 96 . Examining the colorings in these cases reveals that the repetition of 64 64 and 96 96 is no coincidence. In all colorings with loss 64 64 , the set of monochromatic edges was precisely for some y ∈ { 1 , 2 } y\in\{1,2\} . In all colorings with loss 96 96 , it was precisely up to permuting coordinates 2 2 through 7 7 . In the hypercube graph with r = 7 r=7 , the six colorings with loss 64 64 had an analogous form, and a similar pattern held for many of the other r r values. The first of these colorings is the 7 7 -dimensional analog of the colorings shown in Figure 6 .
